content.subject: Reading list request — foundational PI cases
content.body:
Hi everyone,

Quick personal request that's a little outside the normal case stuff. As some of you know, I started evening classes at the local law school this past January, mostly out of curiosity after my own product-liability matter wrapped up last summer. I'm thoroughly hooked. My first-year torts professor moves fast and assumes everyone has done the background reading, and I am very much not at that level yet.

Would someone at the firm be willing to put together a short reading list of the foundational personal-injury cases that any first-year student should have under their belt? I'm thinking the leading authorities on negligence, the seminal decisions on duty and foreseeability, and a few of the classic product-liability rulings. Maybe ten to fifteen cases total with the full citations so I can pull them on Westlaw at the school library. If anyone wants to add a one-line note about why each one matters, that would be incredible, but I don't want to make extra work.

I know this isn't billable and I'm happy to grab lunch for whoever puts it together. Attorney Park mentioned that the firm has done these kinds of reading lists for summer clerks in the past, so I'm hoping it isn't too heavy a lift.

Appreciate it,
Devon
